topic: Why do we get goosebumps? (the fur reflex you no longer need)
research_summary: Candidates (score out of 40: curiosity, universality, timeliness, search, surprise, visual, shareability, verifiability): (1) Why we get goosebumps, a reflex for fur we no longer have: 36 (5,5,3,4,5,4,5,5). (2) Why winter static shocks happen: 35 (rejected by the variety guard: Science Explained was used in the last two videos and the last video was a close touch/physics cousin). (3) Why prices end in 99 before Black Friday: 33 (no controlled study found to confirm numbers). Also considered: UPI in two seconds 33, why Delhi fog forms 30, why we shiver 29. Winner: goosebumps. Highest score, Human Body is not cooling down, and the hook 'your body keeps trying to fluff up fur you don't have' is a genuine surprise. Timely because winter is arriving across north India (dense fog and a western disturbance around 9-15 Nov per IMD and Down To Earth reports); otherwise evergreen. How it works: cold or strong emotion triggers the sympathetic nervous system; a tiny arrector pili muscle at the base of each hair contracts, pulls the hair upright, and the skin bunches into a bump. An adult has roughly five million hair follicles (approximate, counts vary by source), each with its own muscle. In furry mammals the raised fur traps insulating air or makes the animal look bigger; in humans the sparse hair barely warms us, so most researchers consider the reflex a leftover from furry ancestors. Newer ideas (sebum release, hair stem cells) are speculative and left out. Analogy: a puffer jacket. Sources: LiveScience 'Why do we get goosebumps?'; Wikipedia 'Goose bumps' (Pilomotor); Sciencing on the arrector pili. Facts taken from search summaries of these pages.

english.title: Why Do We Get Goosebumps? It's a Fur Reflex
english.description: Goosebumps are a reflex built for fur your body no longer has. Here is how a tiny muscle at the base of every hair turns cold, fear or a great song into bumps. #goosebumps #humanbody #science #howitworks

scenes.text: Your body keeps trying to fluff up fur you don't have.
You've felt it in cold air, or a scary scene. Goosebumps. But why?
Your skin feels the cold. Your brain fires an alarm down tiny nerves to one hair. Now it gets weird.
Every hair has a tiny muscle. The alarm makes it squeeze. The hair stands up, the skin bunches into a bump.
You have roughly five million hairs. Five million tiny muscles, squeezing at once.
In furry animals, it fluffs the fur and traps warm air, like a puffer jacket. Scared? It makes them look bigger.
Strong feelings fire the same alarm, so songs give you chills. Goosebumps: your body fluffing up fur you don't have.
So when you shiver tonight, remember the fur you don't have. Follow to understand one new thing every day.

hindi.title: रोंगटे खड़े क्यों होते हैं? यह फ़र वाला पुराना रिफ़्लेक्स है
hindi.description: रोंगटे खड़े होना उस फ़र के लिए बना रिफ़्लेक्स है, जो अब आपके शरीर पर नहीं है। जानिए हर बाल की जड़ की नन्ही मांसपेशी ठंड, डर या गाने को उभार में कैसे बदलती है। #रोंगटे #humanbody #विज्ञान #hindi

scenes.text: आपका शरीर उस फ़र को फुलाता है, जो आपके पास नहीं।
ठंड हो या डर, रोंगटे खड़े हो जाते हैं। पर क्यों?
त्वचा ठंड महसूस करती है। दिमाग़ नसों से अलार्म भेजता है, सीधे एक बाल तक। अब अजीब हिस्सा।
हर बाल की जड़ में नन्ही मांसपेशी है। अलार्म से वह सिकुड़ती है, बाल खड़ा होता है, त्वचा उभरती है।
शरीर पर लगभग पचास लाख बाल हैं, यानी पचास लाख मांसपेशियाँ, एक साथ।
जानवरों में यह फ़र फुलाकर गर्म हवा रोकता है, पफ़र जैकेट जैसे।
यही अलार्म भावनाओं में भी बजता है। रोंगटे खड़े होना: उस फ़र को फुलाता शरीर, जो आपके पास नहीं।
जब ठंड लगे, तो उस फ़र को याद करें, जो नहीं है। रोज़ एक नई चीज़ समझने के लिए फ़ॉलो करें।
